model: 20/40/40 pools; position cap 9% of its pool; inverse allocation 0%; selection is a monitoring universe, not an entry signal.

stocks.label: S&P 500
stocks.rationale: Lowest measured volatility among the selected broad equity candidates; use as the market baseline.

stocks.label: Nasdaq 100
stocks.rationale: Liquid growth exposure; its 0.93 correlation with SPY means these are overlapping equity risks.

stocks.label: Russell 2000
stocks.rationale: Adds a small-cap comparison with lower measured drawdown than the higher-volatility tech candidates.

stocks.label: Health care
stocks.rationale: Lower measured volatility and 0.22 correlation with SPY in the reviewed year.

stocks.label: Apple
stocks.rationale: Liquid fractional stock with a smaller measured one-year drawdown than MSFT, AMZN, GOOGL and META.

stocks.label: JPMorgan Chase
stocks.rationale: Adds financial-sector coverage with lower measured volatility than the selected tech stock.

stocks.label: ExxonMobil
stocks.rationale: Adds energy coverage; negative correlation with SPY in this sample is descriptive, not a guaranteed hedge.

stocks.label: Gold trust
stocks.rationale: Adds gold-price exposure, but its 26% drawdown rules out treating it as a low-risk cash substitute.

stocks.label: NVIDIA
stocks.rationale: Liquid active-trading research candidate; higher volatility means tighter risk review, not a larger position.

stocks.label: Short S&P 500
stocks.rationale: Daily -1x S&P 500 objective; inverse allocation is still zero and multi-day results can diverge from -1x.

crypto.label: Bitcoin
crypto.rationale: Crypto reference; reviewed drawdown exceeds 50%. Fees and execution costs must pass testing before entry.

crypto.label: Ethereum
crypto.rationale: Second crypto reference; reviewed drawdown exceeds 65%. Keep the same pool/position caps and test costs first.
